pills.text: HUMAN RIGHTS, CIVIL LIBERTIES AND DEMOCRATIC RIGHTS
CENTRAL FOCUS
[1] HUMAN RIGHTS ATTACH TO PERSONS THROUGH DIGNITY AND
[2] CIVIL LIBERTIES PROTECT LEGAL FREEDOM AGAINST ARBITRARY PUBLIC
[3] DEMOCRATIC RIGHTS ENABLE CITIZENS TO PARTICIPATE IN COLLECTIVE
[4] THE CATEGORIES OVERLAP BUT ARE NOT ARRANGED IN
RIGHTS CATEGORIES OVERLAP BECAUSE DIGNITY, LIBERTY AND PARTICIPATION INTERDEPEND.
ANSWER USE

sequence: CENTRAL FOCUS
Human Rights, Civil Liberties and Democratic Rights
[1] Human rights attach to persons through dignity and universal moral concern.
[2] Civil liberties protect legal freedom against arbitrary public power.
[3] Democratic rights enable citizens to participate in collective self-government.

stages.title: NATURAL, LEGAL, HISTORICAL AND PERSONALITY THEORIES

pills.text: NATURAL, LEGAL, HISTORICAL AND PERSONALITY THEORIES
CENTRAL FOCUS
[1] NATURAL-RIGHTS THEORIES GIVE CLAIMS MORAL FORCE BEFORE LEGAL
[2] LEGAL THEORIES STRESS PUBLIC DEFINITION, GUARANTEE AND ENFORCEABILITY.
[3] HISTORICAL THEORIES GROUND RIGHTS IN EVOLVED PRACTICES AND
[4] PERSONALITY THEORIES CONNECT RIGHTS TO MORAL DEVELOPMENT AND

ANSWER USE

Natural, Legal, Historical and Personality Theories

[2] Legal theories stress public definition, guarantee and enforceability.
[3] Historical theories ground rights in evolved practices and inheritance.

stages.title: BURKE, LASKI, MARX AND NOZICK

pills.text: BURKE, LASKI, MARX AND NOZICK
CENTRAL FOCUS
[1] BURKE PROTECTS PRESCRIPTIVE INHERITANCE BUT RISKS PRESERVING INHERITED
[2] LASKI TREATS RIGHTS AS SOCIAL CONDITIONS OF PERSONALITY
[3] MARX EXPOSES CLASS POWER BENEATH FORMALLY EQUAL RIGHTS.
[4] NOZICK DEFENDS SIDE-CONSTRAINTS AND AN ANTI-REDISTRIBUTIVE MINIMAL STATE.
RIGHTS CAN PROTECT AGENCY AND STILL CONCEAL UNEQUAL SOCIAL
ANSWER USE

sequence: CENTRAL FOCUS
Burke, Laski, Marx and Nozick
[1] Burke protects prescriptive inheritance but risks preserving inherited exclusion.
[2] Laski treats rights as social conditions of personality and common welfare.
[3] Marx exposes class power beneath formally equal rights.

stages.title: GENERATIONS OF RIGHTS AND INDIVISIBILITY

pills.text: GENERATIONS OF RIGHTS AND INDIVISIBILITY
CENTRAL FOCUS
[1] FIRST-GENERATION RIGHTS PROTECT CIVIL AND POLITICAL AGENCY BUT
[2] SECOND-GENERATION RIGHTS CONTAIN PROGRESSIVE AND IMMEDIATE OBLIGATIONS.
[3] THIRD-GENERATION CLAIMS HAVE UNEQUAL LEGAL STATUS AND ENFORCEMENT
[4] INDIVISIBILITY MEANS MUTUAL SUPPORT, NOT IDENTICAL DUTIES OR
GENERATIONS ORGANISE CLAIMS BUT CANNOT RANK OR DATE THEM
ANSWER USE

sequence: CENTRAL FOCUS
Generations of Rights and Indivisibility

[2] Second-generation rights contain progressive and immediate obligations.
[3] Third-generation claims have unequal legal status and enforcement paths.

stages.title: NUREMBERG, UDHR, ICCPR AND ICESCR

pills.text: NUREMBERG, UDHR, ICCPR AND ICESCR
CENTRAL FOCUS
[1] THE UDHR IS A GLOBAL STANDARD RATHER THAN
[2] ICCPR DUTIES STRESS RESPECT, ENSURE AND EFFECTIVE REMEDY.
[3] ICESCR COMBINES PROGRESSIVE REALISATION WITH IMMEDIATE NON-DISCRIMINATION AND
[4] NUREMBERG SUPPLIED AN ACCOUNTABILITY PRECEDENT, NOT THE WHOLE
HUMAN-RIGHTS INSTRUMENTS DIFFER IN FORM, DUTY AND ENFORCEMENT ROUTE.
ANSWER USE

sequence: CENTRAL FOCUS
Nuremberg, UDHR, ICCPR and ICESCR
[1] The UDHR is a global standard rather than a treaty with Covenant form.
[2] ICCPR duties stress respect, ensure and effective remedy.
[3] ICESCR combines progressive realisation with immediate non-discrimination and steps.

stages.title: RESTRICTIONS, EMERGENCIES, HORIZONTAL EFFECT AND PROTECTION

pills.text: RESTRICTIONS, EMERGENCIES, HORIZONTAL EFFECT AND PROTECTION
CENTRAL FOCUS
[1] ORDINARY RESTRICTIONS REQUIRE LAW, PERMITTED AIM, NECESSITY AND
[2] EMERGENCY DEROGATION IS NARROWER AND LEAVES SPECIFIED NON-DEROGABLE
[3] HORIZONTAL HARMS MAY REQUIRE LEGISLATION OR POSITIVE STATE
[4] THE NHRC DETENTION CASE IS AN ALLEGATION AND
LAWFUL LIMITS AND EMERGENCY DEROGATION REQUIRE SEPARATE STRUCTURED TESTS.
ANSWER USE

sequence: CENTRAL FOCUS
Restrictions, Emergencies, Horizontal Effect and Protection
[1] Ordinary restrictions require law, permitted aim, necessity and proportionality.
[2] Emergency derogation is narrower and leaves specified non-derogable rights intact.
[3] Horizontal harms may require legislation or positive state protection.
